mechanism_narrative: The observed consistent upward trend in RETAIL_REC over the last four weeks indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity, which will continue to drive mobility higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in transit station activity, moving closer to baseline, signals a return to pre-pandemic commuting and leisure travel patterns, which will boost retail and recreation visits in the short term.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT mobility rises above -30% from baseline and stays there for at least one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show an increase over the next 14 days despite TRANSIT mobility rising above -30% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: As workplace attendance continues to recover and residential mobility declines, it suggests a shift from home-based activities to out-of-home routines, which will collectively drive an increase in retail and recreation visits over the coming month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, or WORKPLACES mobility declines while RESIDENTIAL mobility increases.

mechanism_narrative: The recent dip in parks mobility after a period of recovery, combined with the late summer timing, suggests a temporary shift away from outdoor leisure, which will redirect some recreational spending towards indoor retail activities in the immediate short term.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility drops by more than 2 points week-on-week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 7 days, or PARKS mobility recovers sharply above -19%.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in residential mobility over the past four weeks indicates a sustained reduction in time spent at home, directly correlating with an increase in out-of-home activities, thereby driving retail and recreation mobility upwards.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases or stabilizes while RETAIL_REC mobility declines over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained recovery in workplace attendance, evidenced by WORKPLACES mobility consistently above -12% from baseline, signifies a return to daily commuting patterns that will gradually increase demand for retail and recreation services during workdays over the next month.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES mobility remains above -12% from baseline for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show a sustained increase over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES mobility remaining above -12%.

mechanism_narrative: The stable and slightly increasing grocery and pharmacy visits, combined with the upward trend in retail and recreation, suggests a broader increase in essential and discretionary out-of-home activities, reinforcing the positive momentum for retail over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility declines while RETAIL_REC also declines over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: In the absence of new public health restrictions, the current upward trajectory of general mobility, particularly in transit and workplaces, will continue to foster an environment conducive to increased retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:No new public health restrictions announced by 2022-08-15
failure_condition: New public health restrictions are introduced, or RETAIL_REC declines despite stable or increasing TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility.
